newsitem.title: USA: NU sees little change in capital outlays.
newsitem.headline: NU sees little change in capital outlays.

text.p: Northeast Utilities sees little change in capital spending next year, according to the utility's interim financial forecast and review.

The company said it now expects 1997 outlays of $262 million, little changed from this year's $260 million, as an increase in Connecticut Light and Power Co spending is offset by declines at Public Service Co of New Hampshire and Western Massachusetts Electric Co.
Director of Investor Relations Jeffrey R. Kotkin pointed out that capital spending does not include the outlays on the company's nuclear plants, which is considered maintenance.
For the final three years of the 20th century, NU sees declining capital spending -- to $240 million in 1998, $226 million in 1999 and $218 million in 2000.

The forecast put NU'S retail electric sales at 30.97 billion kilowatthours reflecting the company's previously announced expectation that sales would increase 1.4 percent this year. Next year's expected 0.7 percent increase would put retail sales at 31.41 billion kilowatt hours, it said.
The forecast also includes a projection of the system's regulatory assets and acquisition premiums, projecting a 1996 year end total of $2.45 billion.
Kotkin said this includes $2 billion of regulatory assets as forecast in the company's 1995 annual report.
He said the latest publication combined the two numbers to show that both of these indications of stranded assets are declining.
The total for 1997 year-end is put at $2.33 billion, declining to $2.02 billion at the end of 1998, $1.69 billion in 1999 and $1.35 billion in 2000.
